page: Microsoft Azure E96-24ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The configuration provides 24 virtual CPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 672.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 28.0 GB per core.

This server includes 3686 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, allowing for high-speed local data access. It does not feature any GPU accelerators. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (specifically avx512f and avx512_vnni) for vector operations, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the average tier for general compute tasks, with a single-core stress-ng score of 1899.88 and a multi-core score of 23302.71. However, its memory subsystem exhibits strong performance, particularly in large-block write operations at 108.01 GB/sec and the Passmark memory benchmark, both ranking in the top 25%. Conversely, due to the lack of GPU acceleration, large-scale AI workloads like LLM inference on a 70B model perform poorly, registering only 4.85 tokens per second.

Given its high memory density relative to the vCPU count, the E96-24ds_v5 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that are memory-bound rather than compute-bound. This makes it highly suitable for large in-memory databases, caching layers, enterprise applications, and data analytics pipelines that require substantial RAM and local SSD scratch space without requiring massive parallel CPU scaling.
